The first part asks for P(A) times P(B), the product of two probabilities. Your 0.667 looks like it matches one of those two probabilities by itself. If the product equalled one factor, the other factor would have to be 1, which would mean that event always happens. Does the roll being even always happen? Reconcile that with your result.

Your 0.667 is not right, and the same number came out twice. Here is a test of it. Multiplying two probabilities that are each below 1 must give something smaller than both. Is 0.667 smaller than P(A) for the even roll? Check that, and tell me what you think went into 0.667.

Your steps so far are right. But 1.05 can't be a probability, since none can exceed 1. Also, the three posteriors must add to 1, and the coin being type A is only one of three options. Look at what you put on top of the fraction for type A. Is it the same kind of quantity as the 0.16 you found for type B?
